title: Stamping extends the visited span
statement: Let $M$ be a finite Boolean Turing machine, let $c$ be a configuration of $M$ on a Boolean input, and let $\ell_i,h_i\in\mathbb{Z}$ be bounds for each work tape $i$. Suppose $\ell_i\le h_i$ and $\ell_i-1\le p_i\le h_i+1$, where $p_i$ is the head position on tape $i$. One step of the tracked machine from the intermediate stamping configuration equals the completed tracked configuration of $c$, with each span extended to include $p_i$ by replacing its bounds with $\min(\ell_i,p_i)$ and $\max(h_i,p_i)$.
hypotheses_covered: $M$ is a finite Boolean Turing machine
$c$ is a configuration of $M$ on a Boolean input
replaced:
Let $c$ be a source configuration with visited bounds $\ell_i \le h_i$ such that each
head of $c$ lies within one cell of its span. One step of the tracked evaluator from the
intermediate stamp configuration of $c$ equals the completed tracked configuration of
$c$ with each span extended to include the current head, after which the stored
successor control (possibly a halt) is dispatched.
